title: Unbounded Thread Block on Resource Pool Checkout
damaged_code:
```rust
// Rust (tokio or r2d2)
let conn = pool.get(); // Blocks indefinitely until a connection is available
```
pattern: Attempting to check out a resource from a thread or connection pool without specifying a timeout.
why_bad: If the database or remote service crashes or experiences a severe latency spike, connection checkouts block indefinitely. This quickly exhausts the request-handling thread pool, turning a localized database slowdown into a complete application freeze [160, 201].
detection: Identify invocations of connection pool checkouts (e.g., `.get()`, `.checkout()`, `pool.acquire()`) where no timeout argument is supplied, or where the pool configuration sets the checkout timeout to infinite/none.
counterexample:
```rust
let conn = pool.get_timeout(Duration::from_secs(2)); // Fails fast if unavailable
```
fix: Ensure every resource checkout has a strict, bounded timeout, allowing the request-handling thread to fail fast and release capacity.
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, page 81, 111-114, 201 / passage [160, 201].
